Klondike on NoCharge: Rules and Rhythm

Current Klondike rules on NoCharge: a seeded deal, draw-one or draw-three mode, move count, and no saved record or undo control.

By NoCharge·Reviewed by NoCharge·Published August 22, 2026·Updated November 24, 2026·2 min read
Try the detail in a live board.

Classic solitaire. Draw one or three.

Play Klondike SolitaireBrowse all Articles

Bottom line: NoCharge Klondike uses a fixed seeded deal, seven tableau columns, four suit foundations, and a stock-and-waste pile. You can switch between drawing one or three cards during a deal; there is no timer or saved win record.

Build the tableau and foundations

Tableau runs descend by rank in alternating colors. Only a King can start an empty column. Foundations begin with Aces and build upward by suit. The current page shows the stock, the top waste card, each foundation, and seven tableau columns.

Draw one or three

The Draw selector switches between one-card and three-card draws. The setting can be changed while the deal is in progress. When the stock is empty, activating it recycles the waste into the stock. The deal itself is deterministic: Reset to seeded start restores the same layout.

What the counter means

The current page displays a move count as you play. It is not a saved best-move record or a leaderboard. The current V2 interface has no Undo button, win-history dashboard, or timer. If a deal is difficult or you reach a point with no useful move, you can continue considering the layout or reset it; the game does not label the deal winnable or unwinnable.

Keep the claim narrow

This article describes the controls and rules in the current build. It makes no solvability-rate claim and does not promise that every seeded deal can be won. For another solitaire layout with all cards face up, compare FreeCell on NoCharge.
